rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Health and safety law applies to film, television and broadcasting work activities in the UK, including unpaid work.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Legal health-and-safety duties cannot be delegated away by a producer or production company.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Productions must define responsibilities and duties for managing health and safety.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: A production needs a health-and-safety management system proportionate to its size and complexity.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Production activities must be systematically assessed for hazards and exposure risks.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Controls should eliminate production hazards where possible or reduce them where elimination is not practicable.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Risk assessments and controls must be reviewed and updated as production work changes.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Construction work for sets, locations and temporary production structures may engage CDM planning and coordination duties.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Production risk depends on location, set design, vehicles, stunts, pyrotechnics, weapons, weather, freelancers and schedule pressure.

rows.source: HSE film, TV and broadcasting safety
rows.verified: Film and broadcasting evidence is production-, location-, activity-, contractor- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Theatre operators must control risks to workers and people attending productions.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Employers, employees, self-employed workers and people controlling premises all have relevant legal duties.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Theatre employers must assess work risks and eliminate or control them so far as reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Work at height is a major source of theatre-industry injury and must be planned and controlled.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Manual handling is a major theatre risk and should be reduced in amount and severity.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Noise from performances, rehearsals and technical work must be assessed and controlled.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Electrical equipment used at entertainment venues should be selected, installed, operated and maintained to prevent electrical danger.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Temporary construction work for productions requires clear client, designer, contractor and coordination roles where CDM applies.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Theatre risk depends on production design, rigging, scenery, load-in, performance effects, audience layout, competence and time pressure.

rows.source: HSE theatre health and safety
rows.verified: Theatre evidence is venue-, production-, task-, equipment-, audience- and schedule-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
